lessonTitle: How to capture insights during a visit

slides.title: Capture Starts During the Conversation
bullets: Memory degrades fast, and specific phrasing is lost first
Reconstructing a conversation afterward loses the details that carry meaning
Real capture begins in the room, not back at a desk

slides.title: Lightweight Notes That Don't Break Rapport
bullets: Writing everything verbatim pulls focus and makes physicians guarded
Capture key phrases, specific numbers, examples and anything unexpected
Keep it quick enough not to break eye contact for long

slides.title: Separate What Was Said From What You Think
bullets: Mark direct quotes and paraphrases distinctly from personal analysis
Interpretation added later, once memory blurs, is far less reliable
Make the split explicit in the moment, not afterward

slides.title: Specificity Beats Generalisation
bullets: A vague concern is far less useful days later than a specific one
Capture the exact finding, the numbers, the direct question asked
Specificity determines whether it becomes a grounded insight or stays vague

slides.title: Develop Rough Notes While Memory Is Fresh
bullets: Structure the notes the same day, ideally right after the visit
Fill in context and start applying the data-to-implication framework
Delaying even a few days measurably degrades accuracy and completeness

slides.title: Technology Speeds Writeup, Not Listening
bullets: CRM platforms and AI transcription tools reduce the writeup burden
They do not replace listening carefully and noting specifics in the moment
Good tools only work faster once good raw material already exists

takeaway.title: Good insight capture happens live, separates fact from interpretation, and stays specific
bullets: Capture key phrases and specifics during the conversation, not after
Keep quotes and interpretation visibly distinct in the moment
Structure notes the same day while the conversation is still fresh
